title: EU residency pathway orchestrator: tenant safelists and failover semantics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers operating under EU data residency requirements need strong, auditable routing guarantees that their inference traffic and derived artifacts never leave approved EU processing boundaries. Current router supports simple region tags and a tenant allowlist, but we lack a unified runtime "pathway orchestrator" that evaluates multi-clause policies, emits verifiable handoff events, and executes deterministic failover to compliant model variants or a degraded service tier.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway Orchestrator evaluates tenant legal profile + request metadata and returns a deterministic routing decision (eu-hosted | eu-fallback-variant | non-eu-block) for 100% of test cases
Per-request audit event is emitted with decision rationale (policy clauses hit, precedence order, TTL on cached decision) and visible in Console trace view
Tenant safelist/denylist API is implemented and governed by RBAC; changes appear in config within 30s and are honored by runtime within 60s

Fallback semantics: when EU capacity constrained, requests are routed to an EU-compatible quantized variant or enqueued per policy; unacceptable escapes produce a hard block with clear user-facing error code
Automated end-to-end tests that simulate consent headers, explicit tenant residency flags, and emergency 'escape' scenarios with expected routing outcomes
technical_design:
Overview:
- Introduce a Pathway Orchestrator service that sits in the pre-routing layer. It accepts enriched request metadata (tenant_id, consent_headers, customer_policy_version, inferred_jurisdiction) and evaluates a policy graph to produce a routing token.
- Policy evaluation engine is ordered: explicit tenant safelist/denylist -> tenant legal_profile (residency_required) -> consent header (opt-in/out) -> emergency override -> default region mapping. Each clause emits a structured rationale string used for auditing.
- Cache: decisions are cached keyed by (tenant_id, policy_version, request_signature) with a TTL of 10s by default; cache entries are invalidated on safelist/denylist updates.
- Failover: fallback model variants are annotated in model catalog with compliance tags (eu_compliant, eu_resident_copy). Orchestrator will select the highest-priority variant within the same compartment; if none, apply configured policy (queue, block, or degrade to embeddings-only).
- Auditing: every decision writes a compact audit record to customer-scoped audit stream (append-only with sequence id) and also emits a trace event for Console. Records include: decision_id, tenant_id, policy_clause_hits, candidate_variants, chosen_variant, cache_hit, timestamp, and operator (if manual override).
- RBAC/Config: safelist/denylist exposed via Console and an admin API; changes require 'policy.admin' role and forward to config-store with optimistic concurrency.
- Backward compatibility: router falls back to the existing region tagger when orchestrator is disabled via feature flag.
Implementation notes:
- Language: Go for orchestrator core (matches runtime components) with a thin Rust evaluator lib possible later for speed.
- Performance target: <1ms median overhead for policy eval under normal cache hit rates, 95th <5ms.
- Telemetry: counters for decisions by clause, latency histograms, cache hit rate, and blocked_request_rate.
- Config storage: existing config service (kv-store) with versioned policy blobs.
- Safety: implement a circuit-breaker that prevents automated fallback to non-EU endpoints if past an emergency threshold (blocked_request_rate > 0.5% over 1m).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy orchestrator behind feature flag for 1 internal tenant and 5 pilot customers in eu-west with auditing enabled; monitor metrics and Console traces
Phase 2 (gradual): enable for 10% of EU traffic after 72h stable canary, expose Admin UI for safelist edits to platform ops
Phase 3 (enforce): default enforcement for new tenants; provide opt-in migration for existing tenants with advisory notices
Phase 4 (global): enable APIs for dedicated/private deployments with KMS-enforced audit streams
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence matrix and individual clause evaluators
Integration tests that spin up router + orchestrator + model-catalog mock; assert chosen_variant and audit events
Chaos test: simulate EU capacity pressure and verify fallback routing and queuing behavior
Compliance test: synthetic traffic with varying consent/jurisdiction headers to assert hard-block outcomes
Performance test: p95 evaluation latency under 1000 rps; cache hit/miss scenarios
migration_notes: For existing tenants we will run a rolling check that computes a 'residency_score' using historical traffic and tenant settings. Tenants with residency_score>0.9 will be recommended to opt-in to strict enforcement. Admin UI will provide a one-click migration; behind the scenes we will backfill the policy_version and seed the orchestrator cache to avoid cold-start spikes.
risks: Mis-evaluations if tenant policy blobs are stale — mitigated by optimistic invalidation hooks and versioned policies
Operator error when editing safelists — mitigated by RBAC + change review + 30s staging window before enforcement
Performance regressions at high QPS — mitigate with caching, rate-limiters, and a fast-path for trivial decisions
Audit exposure: audit stream must be encrypted and access-controlled to avoid PII leaks
